html:
The Gujarat Sultanate ruled western India from 1407 to 1573. On the 1492 map it is at its peak under Sultan Mahmud Begada.

Its founder was the governor of Gujarat for the Delhi Sultanate, who declared himself independent. His grandson Ahmad Shah founded Ahmedabad in 1411, a capital famous for its mosques with carved stone screens. Mahmud Begada, who ruled from 1458 to 1511, took the hill forts of Junagadh and Pavagadh and built a new city at Champaner.

Gujarat lived by the sea. Its ports, Cambay, Surat and Diu, sent cotton cloth and indigo across the Indian Ocean. When the Portuguese arrived, the sultan joined the Mamluks of Egypt against them, but their fleet lost the Battle of Diu in 1509, and Portugal later took Diu itself. In 1573 Akbar conquered Gujarat for the Mughals.
sum: The Gujarat Sultanate ruled western India from 1407 to 1573. On the 1492 map it is at its peak under Sultan Mahmud Begada.
